{{Short description|Mathematical function}}
[[File:Buchstab-function-graph-from-1-to-4.png|300px|thumbnail|Graph of the Buchstab function ''ω''(''u'') from ''u''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 to ''u''&nbsp;=&nbsp;4.]]
The '''Buchstab function''' (or '''Buchstab's function''') is the unique continuous function <math>\omega: \R_{\ge 1}\rightarrow \R_{>0}</math> defined by the [[delay differential equation]]
:<math>\omega(u)=\frac 1 u, \qquad\qquad\qquad 1\le u\le 2,</math>
:<math>{\frac{d}{du}} (u\omega(u))=\omega(u-1), \qquad u\ge 2.</math>
In the second equation, the derivative at ''u''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 should be taken as ''u'' approaches 2 from the right. It is named after [[Alexander Buchstab]], who wrote about it in 1937.

==Asymptotics==
The Buchstab function approaches <math>e^{-\gamma} \approx 0.561</math> rapidly as <math>u\to\infty,</math> where <math>\gamma</math> is the [[Euler–Mascheroni constant]].  In fact,

:<math>|\omega(u)-e^{-\gamma}|\le \frac{\rho(u-1)}{u}, \qquad u\ge 1,</math>

where ''ρ''  is the [[Dickman function]].<ref>(5.13), Jurkat and Richert 1965.  In this paper the argument of ''ρ'' has been shifted by 1 from the usual definition.</ref>  Also, <math>\omega(u)-e^{-\gamma}</math> oscillates in a regular way, alternating between extrema and zeroes; the extrema alternate between positive maxima and negative minima.  The interval between consecutive extrema approaches 1 as ''u'' approaches infinity, as does the interval between consecutive zeroes.<ref>p. 131, Cheer and Goldston 1990.</ref>

==Applications==
The Buchstab function is used to count [[rough number]]s.
If Φ(''x'',&nbsp;''y'') is the number of positive integers less than or equal to ''x'' with no prime factor less than ''y'', then for any fixed ''u''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1,
:<math>\Phi(x,x^{1/u}) \sim \omega(u)\frac{x}{\log x^{1/u}}, \qquad x\to\infty.</math>
